repository.name: jobFynder-BE-nestJS
repository.description: This is for BE rewamp to nestJS from nodeJS

commits.message:
fix(resume): whitelist PUT /resume/:id fields and require auth on generate-section

- PUT /resume/:id spread the raw request body into prisma.update, letting a
  caller overwrite id/userId/fileUrl/templateResumeUrl. Now typed as
  UpdateResumeDto and only whitelisted editable fields are written.
- POST /resume/generate-section had no guard (unauthenticated LLM calls).
  Now requires JwtAuthGuard; the FE does not call this route.
- Remove dead null-check after prisma.update (it throws, never returns null).
- Tests: guard coverage for generate-section, whitelist test for updateResume.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(hermes): reject dry-run placeholder resume suggestions with 503

Hermes' /resume-builder summary/bullet endpoints answer 200 with
"[dry-run] Prompt ... rendered successfully" placeholder text when its
prompt runtime is in dry_run. suggestSummary/suggestBullet passed that
straight through, so the resume editor showed it as generated content.
Now it throws ServiceUnavailableError (503) like generateResumeSection.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): add resume variants (label, variantType, parentResumeId)

Second piece of the resume-persistence foundation, on top of this
same PR's auth-guard fix. A "variant" (role-based, job-specific,
company-specific, recruiter-requested, or blind-resume) is just
another `resumes` row -- same content, tagged with a parent and a
type -- not a new table or subsystem.

Schema: additive migration adding `label`, `variantType`, and
`parentResumeId` (self-relation, ON DELETE SET NULL so deleting a
base resume doesn't cascade-delete every variant built from it).
`label` is new because there was no way to give a resume record its
own display name before ("Java Tech Lead - Fintech Focus" as opposed
to `title`, which is the professional headline printed on the resume
itself, e.g. "Senior Java Developer" -- those are different things
and would otherwise collide once a user has more than one resume).

New endpoints, both ownership-checked the same way every other route
here is (only works on a resume the caller already owns):
- POST /resume/:id/variants -- copies :id's content into a new row,
  tagged with parentResumeId=:id, the given label/variantType, and an
  optional targetRole/targetCompany merged into builderMetadata.
- GET /resume/:id/variants -- lists variants of :id.

Extended resume.controller.spec.ts to cover both new routes (8/8
passing). `nest build` / `tsc --noEmit` clean, `prisma generate` picks
up the new fields with no errors. Same caveat as the first commit:
not yet run against a live database.

test(resume): cover variant guards and ownership

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(billing): add multi-tenant subscription/billing module (Stripe-first)

Full first pass at the requested Subscription module: Customer, Plan/
PlanPrice, Subscription, Invoice/InvoiceLineItem, Payment, Coupon,
PaymentMethod, WebhookEvent, and SubscriptionEvent audit trail
(prisma/schema.prisma + migration 20260822020000). Customer binds to
either an Organization or a standalone User (never both) so both
org-level and individual-consultant subscriptions are supported without
forcing solo users into creating an org.

Stripe is fully wired end-to-end (customer/subscription/invoice/payment
creation, webhook ingestion with signature verification + idempotency,
daily dunning retries via the existing ScheduleModule cron). Razorpay
gets the identical PaymentGatewayAdapter interface but every method
throws NotImplementedError -- an explicit, loud stub rather than fake
logic, per the agreed Stripe-first rollout.

Reused existing infrastructure instead of reinventing it:
- org-access/ (CASL-based RBAC) for multi-tenancy -- no new OrgPermission
  codes needed, since employer:billing_manage_subscription /
  employer:billing_view_invoices (and the sp: equivalents) were already
  seeded in org-defaults.ts and unused until now.
- ScheduleModule (already registered in app.module.ts) for the dunning
  cron, matching cron/expire-invitations.service.ts's pattern.
- The three-layer config pattern (env.validation.ts Joi schema ->
  configuration.ts typed block with isConfigured getter -> ConfigService)
  for STRIPE_*/RAZORPAY_* env vars, so the app still boots without
  billing configured.
- MailService.sendEmail for dunning notices, apiResponse/pagination.util
  for controller responses, the resume-intelligence.controller.spec.ts
  guard-reflection pattern for the new spec tests.

Proration is a pure, fully unit-tested ProrationService (upgrade/
downgrade/same-day/zero-length-period cases) -- no gateway calls, so the
math is independently verifiable. Upgrades default to immediate
proration+invoice; downgrades default to taking effect at period end
(both overridable via ChangePlanDto.prorationBehavior), matching Stripe's
own default behavior.

One non-obvious fix: main.ts disables Nest's body parser and wires
json()/urlencoded() manually, which would otherwise consume the webhook
request body before Stripe's signature check can see the raw bytes --
added express.raw() scoped to /api/billing/webhooks ahead of the JSON
parser. Also had to add @CsrfExempt() to both webhook controllers, since
the global CsrfGuard (APP_GUARD) requires a browser Origin/CSRF-cookie
pair that a server-to-server Stripe webhook will never send -- caught by
tracing the guard chain, not by testing against live Stripe traffic
(no credentials in this environment).

Explicitly not built this pass (flagged in the plan, not silently
skipped): Razorpay implementation, tax calculation, multi-currency
conversion, and a billing portal/checkout UI.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full existing jest
suite (127 tests across 23 suites) still passes, plus 27 new tests
(8 ProrationService unit tests, guard/permission-metadata reflection
tests for every new controller). Not verified against a live Stripe/
Razorpay account or a live database -- no credentials or DB connection
in this environment, same caveat as every other backend change this
session.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(credits): add credit ledger, top-up purchases, and gate Resume Builder AI actions

Builds on the Subscription module: CreditGrant (a "lot" of credits with its
own source and expiry) + CreditTransaction (append-only audit trail) +
TopupPack/TopupPurchase (one-off credit-pack purchases via Stripe
PaymentIntents). Balance is always computed live as the sum of non-expired
grants' remaining amounts -- no cached balance field to keep in sync, so
there's no separate "reconcile the balance" bug class to worry about.

Credit sources implemented, all three requested:
- Plan-included, refilled each period: Plan.features.includedCredits
  (already in the Subscription schema, previously unused) is granted via
  SubscriptionService.create() for the first period and
  SubscriptionService.syncFromGateway() for renewals -- both call the same
  idempotent CreditService.grantPlanIncludedCreditsForPeriod(), which checks
  for an existing PLAN_INCLUDED grant created within the current period
  before granting again.
- One-off top-up packs: admin-managed catalog (TopupPack), purchased via a
  new PaymentGatewayAdapter.createOneOffPayment() method (Stripe
  PaymentIntents -- the existing adapter only had subscription-oriented
  methods). Fulfillment happens off the existing payment_intent.succeeded/
  payment_intent.payment_failed webhook handlers, extended to also check
  TopupPurchase (a Payment row lookup alone would miss these, since one-off
  top-ups don't have an Invoice).
- Manual admin grants: POST /billing/credits/customers/:customerId/grant,
  crm_admin only -- also how refunds work when a paid AI call fails after
  credits were already debited.

Expiry (per the "expire at end of billing period" decision): every grant
carries its own expiresAt. Consumption is FIFO by soonest-expiring lot
first (credit-lot-selection.ts, extracted as a pure function specifically
so the ordering/spillover/tie-breaking logic is unit-testable without a
database). A daily cron (CreditExpiryService) zeroes out expired lots'
`remaining` and logs an EXPIRE transaction for reporting -- not required
for balance correctness (getBalance/consume already filter by expiresAt)
but keeps CreditGrant-level numbers and the audit trail honest.

Wired into the first real consumer, per the "Resume Builder AI actions"
decision: tailor, quality/analyze (ATS check), summary/suggest, bullets/
suggest, skills/suggest, and match in resume-intelligence.controller.ts
are now credit-gated -- debited before calling Hermes, refunded if Hermes
fails, hard-reject with InsufficientCreditsError (402) if the balance is
too low. `parse` (resume import/onboarding), `feedback/analyze`, and
`submissions/evaluate` stay free -- the latter two are recruiter/bench-
sales tooling, not consultant AI spend. Per the "blocked until they
subscribe" decision, a user with no Customer record (never subscribed)
gets the same 402 rather than a free allotment.

Costs per action (src/billing/credits/credit-costs.config.ts) are
placeholder numbers -- no product pricing was specified for this pass,
called out explicitly rather than silently invented as if authoritative.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full jest suite (143
tests / 26 suites, up from 127/23) passes -- including 8 new pure-function
tests for the FIFO lot-selection logic and guard/permission-metadata tests
for the two new controllers. Not verified against a live Stripe account or
database, same caveat as the rest of this billing work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(collaboration): resume sharing via link + threaded comments

New module, independent of the billing PRs (#4/#5) -- based on main, no
Subscription/Credits dependency, since sharing/feedback isn't a paid
feature.

ResumeShare (a token-scoped, revocable, optionally-expiring link with
VIEW or COMMENT permission) + ResumeComment (threaded via
parentCommentId, OPEN/RESOLVED status, author is either a platform User
or an anonymous name+email pair for external viewers).

Per the "anyone with a share link" decision: PublicShareController
carries no JwtAuthGuard and no other guard -- the 24-random-byte token
(crypto.randomBytes, same primitive org-invitation.service.ts already
uses for invite tokens, just wider) is the entire access control for
GET .../shared/:token, GET .../shared/:token/comments, and POST
.../shared/:token/comments. Added a deliberate negative test
(public-share.controller.spec.ts) asserting no guard metadata is present
at the class or handler level, specifically so a future edit that
accidentally adds JwtAuthGuard here breaks CI immediately instead of
quietly locking out every logged-out viewer.

Owner-side routes (CollaborationController, JwtAuthGuard) create/list/
revoke share links, list all comments across every share for triage, and
resolve threads -- ownership checked the same way resume.controller.ts
already does it (findFirst({id, userId}), 404 either way so a non-owner
can't distinguish "not found" from "not yours").

Comment posting works both ways: an anonymous viewer through a
COMMENT-permission share link (CreatePublicCommentDto -- authorName
required, authorUserId left null), or the owner themselves replying to
feedback (CreateOwnerCommentDto, authorUserId/authorName from the JWT).
Both paths validate a given parentCommentId actually belongs to the same
resume before threading a reply under it.

Deliberately not built: rich-text/highlight-range anchoring for
quotedText (stored as plain text, no document-position tracking), email
notifications when a comment is posted, and any UI -- backend only, same
as the rest of this session's work.

Verified: tsc --noEmit clean, `nest build` clean, full jest suite (110
tests / 20 suites on this main-based branch) passes, plus 10 new tests
(ShareService token-validation branch coverage, guard-presence checks for
both controllers -- including the negative "no guard" test above). Not
verified against a live database, same caveat as the billing PRs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(credits): give every user 100 starter credits

- New STARTER_GRANT credit source; STARTER_CREDITS = 100.
- StarterCreditService.ensureForUser creates the billing customer locally (no
  payment-gateway call, so it works before Stripe is configured) and grants
  the starter balance once. It is lazy (first credits read / first gated AI
  call) so it covers every existing user without a bulk migration, and
  idempotent via a partial unique index (one starter grant per customer).
- The gateway customer is linked on first purchase (ensureGatewayLink).
- Resume AI gating no longer blocks users that had no billing customer.
- Adds the resume-builder schema (resume documentId/consultantProfileId/
  atsScore, feedback items, skill endorsements, achievements) and migrations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): link resumes to bench consultants and documents

- resumes.consultantProfileId: bench sales can create/list resumes for a
  managed consultant, authorised through the consultants module. Personal and
  consultant resume lists are separate. GET /resume/bench-summary returns
  per-consultant base/variant counts and best ATS score.
- PUT /resume/:id/document links the stored file of record (uploaded through
  the documents module) to a resume, verifying ownership of both.
- parse-resume no longer keeps the uploaded file on local disk.
- UpdateResumeDto/whitelist gain label and atsScore.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): achievement library, feedback and skill endorsements

- /resume-achievements: per-user (or per bench-consultant) reusable bullets;
  list/create/update/delete and usage counting; consultant scope authorised by
  the consultants module.
- /resume/:id/feedback: list, owner notes, status (pending/applied/ignored) and
  POST feedback/analyze, which runs Hermes analysis on the SAVED resume text
  (contact block included) and replaces only PENDING AI items.
- /resume/:id/endorsements (owner) and POST collaboration/shared/:token/
  endorsements (public, COMMENT share links only, idempotent per skill+name).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(hermes): unwrap structured AI suggestions into plain text

Live Hermes answers summary/bullet prompts with a fenced JSON object
(professional_summary / rewritten_bullets). Inserted as-is the editor would
show raw JSON. suggestSummary/suggestBullet now extract the text; plain-text
answers pass through unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(resume): stop accepting file uploads on PUT /resume/:id

The multipart 'template' upload wrote files to local disk (ephemeral, not
private storage) and nothing in the FE or BE used it. Stored files now go only
through the documents module.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(resume): variants inherit the parent's consultantProfileId

A variant created from a bench consultant's resume lost the consultant link,
so it showed up as the bench user's own resume and was not counted in the
bench summary. Found by the local end-to-end run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(resume): bench-consultant resumes without an email; bucket policy script

- Creating a resume for a managed consultant failed with 'email must be an
  email' when the consultant had no email on file, and autosave then failed on
  PUT with an empty email. The email is now optional for consultant resumes
  (taken from the consultant when visible) and an empty email is accepted on
  update. Found by the local role-based end-to-end run.
- scripts/documents-apply-bucket-policy.ts applies the documented CORS +
  7-day lifecycle rules to a quarantine bucket (dry run by default).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): LinkedIn import for the Resume Builder

POST /resume/import/linkedin reuses core's LinkedIn import (scraper, URL
validation, per-user rate limit, linkedin->canonical mapper) and returns a
resume-shaped draft for the builder to review. It does not touch the profile
or create a profile import draft, and invents nothing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(billing): Stripe test/proxy base URL; forged webhook signature is a 400

- STRIPE_API_BASE_URL (optional, test/proxy only) points the Stripe SDK at a
  local mock so the whole top-up flow can be exercised without a key.
- A bad/forged webhook signature now returns 400 instead of 500 (Stripe retries
  5xx). A missing key/secret still reports 503 'not configured'.
- Adapter tests for not-configured, forged and valid signatures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(hermes): default target role, blocked runs, tolerant JSON unwrap

Found by running the AI assists through UAT against live Hermes:
- Hermes blocks a summary/bullet run with no target role (missing job_card);
  that was reported as 'AI not enabled'. A default role is sent when none is
  given and a blocked run is reported as an error.
- The prompts answer with different JSON shapes (accomplishment_bullets with
  rewritten entries, unknown keys); extraction now handles them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): add Jobfynder ATS v1 template to the resume builder

Schema validation (Ajv 2020), lint rules, HTML/TXT/DOCX/PDF renderers, page-fit
trim assistant, builder->template mapper, and /resume/templates endpoints.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): ATS v1 template gaps - keywords, contact override, round-trip, deploy docs

- builder fields: end client, employment type, environment; remote/location parsing; clearer error hints
- keyword analysis against a pasted job description (deterministic, per-sentence weighting)
- contact override and target job flow into the template
- GET /resume/templates reports PDF availability; docs + env example for Chromium
- fix: enableImplicitConversion turned experience/education/certifications objects into arrays on save
- export -> platform text extractor round-trip tests

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): editable ATS preview hooks and fix-it targets for checks

- The server preview can mark editable text (data-bp) and jump targets (data-jump) so the live
  preview edits the right builder field. Exports are unchanged (no markers).
- The mapper records where each mapped row came from (it drops empty bullets, education and
  certifications), and every issue now carries a builder target {section, index, field}.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): real-time sharing and live editing

- People sharing by email with viewer / commenter / editor roles, plus edit-level share links.
- Socket.IO gateway (/resume-collab) relaying a Yjs document, with presence, role pushes and removal.
- Field-level merge: concurrent edits to different fields, bullets and rows all survive.
- Sharing endpoints, shared-with-me, and a save route for editors who do not own the resume.
- Migration adds EDIT, resume_collaborators and resume_collab_docs. Docs in docs/resume/live-collaboration.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(resume): comments, versions, activity trail, section locks, idle timeout, bullet metrics, job import

- Field-anchored comments with replies and resolve, pushed live to open editors (/field-comments).
- Named versions with restore (an automatic version is saved first; the live document is reset).
- Activity trail and per-section last editor; repeated saves coalesce.
- Owner-only section locks enforced on REST saves and on live updates (scratch-copy probe).
- Idle connections are closed after RESUME_COLLAB_IDLE_MS (default 30 min).
- Per-bullet metrics accepted by the ATS mapper.
- POST /resume/job-source/import for LinkedIn Jobs, Dice and careers pages, guarded against internal addresses.
- Migration 20261113200000_resume_history_and_locks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(resume): bullets on import, refuse missing job pages, staging R2 and Hermes tooling

- Hermes import returns each role's duties as one run-on description; split it into bullets
  (abbreviation-safe) so the builder, ATS checks and bullet metrics have content to work on.
- Job-link import refuses error pages ("can't be found", HTTP ERROR 404, "doesn't exist") and
  near-empty text with a plain 400 instead of analysing them as a job.
- Add scripts to set up and check the staging R2 buckets (secrets are prompted for and written to
  .env, never printed), apply quarantine CORS, and point the API at the live Hermes.
- Document the staging R2 / Hermes runbook and the new import behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(linkedin): plain message when LinkedIn import is not configured, add token setup script

The Apify client leaked the setting name ("APIFY_TOKEN is not configured") to users of both
onboarding and the resume builder. Log the detail and return a plain message instead.
Add scripts/setup-linkedin-import.ps1, which prompts for the token (hidden) and writes it to .env.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(resume): security and scale hardening from the PR review (blockers and follow-ups)

Blockers
- Invites only apply to accounts with a verified email (registration issues a token before verification,
  so anyone could register an invited address and read the resume).
- Job import SSRF: one shared address check (IPv4 inside IPv6, NAT64, 6to4, link/unique-local, ports 80/443)
  used for the URL and again for every request the headless browser makes (redirects, images, scripts).
- Job import runs on one shared browser (2 pages at once, bounded queue) with a per-user rate limit.
- Live sockets: sessions and access re-checked every 60 s (sign-out, expired/revoked link, role change);
  non-owners cannot seed while a section is locked; document size capped (1 MB); per-connection message
  budget; connection/room caps; read-only roles refused first; room lease table so a second API instance
  refuses a room another instance owns (new migration resume_collab_leases).

Follow-ups
- Viewers see names, not emails or account ids (comments, history, document, presence); `mine` flag on comments.
- UUID validation on every id; production Prisma errors no longer name columns; 413/400 for bad bodies.
- Share token travels in X-Share-Token and is redacted from request and error logs.
- Caps and pruning for versions, activity, comments, collaborators; batched activity writes; restore in a
  transaction; cursor pagination for comments and shared-with-me.
- PDF render queue cap, per-user render/export limits, 2 MB body limit on rendering/collaboration routes.
- Persistence every 3 s, bounded lock cache, batched role re-checks, cached handshake lookups, merged presence.
- Unused variable fix in resume.util; tests for all of the above; docs and .env.example updated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Resume AI: wire tailor/gaps/cover-letter/headline prompts, output contracts, 429 handling, fair credit prices

- New routes tailor/rewrite, gaps/analyze, cover-letter/generate, headline/suggest with checked output (resume-ai-output)
- Explicit JSON output contract sent with the three prompts that name no format
- Hermes 429: retry after Retry-After (capped) and a per-instance limit on concurrent model calls
- Rule-based features (tailor guidance, quality, skills, match) cost 1 credit; model features keep their price
- No source_text on the new prompts (asserted in tests); prompt registry check script and docs

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: resume AI output schema now lives in the Langfuse prompts (v2)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Resume builder: address architecture review (P0/P1)

- Optimistic concurrency: expectedUpdatedAt on both save endpoints, atomic check+write, 409 on mismatch
- Deleting a resume closes its live room and removes connected people
- atsScore no longer client-writable; stored by the quality check from the analysis
- Linking a document and storing the score no longer move updatedAt
- GET /resume paginated (limit/cursor); bench-summary grouped in the database
- Index on users(lower(email)) for collaborator lookups
- Docs list what is still open (service/envelope refactor, Redis, export-from, JSON validation)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Resume builder: ResumeService + envelope alignment, optional Redis for multi-instance (review P2)

- ResumeService holds the resume rules; ResumeCrudController is the thin HTTP layer on the standard envelope (AppError, ParseUUIDPipe)
- One shared writable-field list (resume-fields.ts) for owner and collaborator saves
- Optional Redis (REDIS_URL): rate limits counted across instances (enforceLimit, atomic script, falls back in-process), access/lock/notify events shared on a pub/sub channel
- Docs: running several instances, sticky routing by resumeId, why no Socket.IO adapter

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Resume builder: finish review follow-ups (export from saved resume, content validation, shared socket cap, bounded uploads)

- POST /resume/:id/export renders from the stored resume for anyone who may view it, 422 on blocking errors, records the export in activity
- Save/create validate content shape and size (422 with reasons); unknown keys pass
- Per-user live-editing socket cap counted across instances via Redis (expiring entries, fails open)
- PDF/DOCX text extraction bounded (RESUME_PARSE_CONCURRENCY / RESUME_PARSE_MAX_QUEUE, 429 beyond)
- Docs: worker-queue decision and its trigger

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
